note: Author-written for Experiment AI (not from the survey). Each pair is a combination of answers most philosophers would treat as inconsistent. 'contestable' marks pairs with a live defended position on the other side; the analysis reports results with and without them.

constraints.why: Physicalism says the physical facts fix the mental facts, so a physical duplicate without consciousness is impossible.
Dualism about consciousness is a form of non-physicalism.
Identity theory identifies conscious states with physical states, which is physicalism.
Eliminativism denies non-physical mental states altogether; it is a physicalist view.
Most panpsychism posits fundamental mentality beyond the physical, though Russellian versions claim to be physicalist.
If zombies are possible, physical-functional facts leave consciousness unexplained, which is the hard problem.
Dualism is motivated by and presupposes an explanatory gap between the physical and consciousness.
Eliminativists deny there is phenomenal consciousness for a hard problem to be about.
Idealism holds reality is fundamentally mental, the opposite of physicalism.
Skepticism about the external world denies we know the observable world, let alone the approximate truth of theories about unobservables.
Error theory says all positive moral claims are false, which denies moral realism.
Expressivism is an anti-realist view of moral claims (quasi-realists dispute the label only in a minimal sense).
Non-naturalism is a form of moral realism.
Naturalist realism is a form of moral realism.
Error theory treats moral judgments as truth-apt beliefs (all false), which is cognitivism.
Expressivism is the standard form of non-cognitivism.
Realism needs moral judgments to state truths; non-cognitivism denies they are beliefs.
Design by an intelligent creator requires a designer, which atheism denies.
Presentism privileges the present, which requires an A-theory of time.
The growing block has an objectively moving present edge, an A-theoretic feature.
Moving-spotlight views combine an A-theory with eternalism, but most A-theorists reject eternalism.
Rationalism holds that some substantive knowledge comes from reason alone, which requires a priori knowledge.
In classical logic a true contradiction entails everything; accepting actual true contradictions requires a paraconsistent logic.
Humeanism reduces nomic and causal facts to the mosaic of particular facts; primitive causation is a non-Humean posit.
On the biological view you are an organism, and an organism is not continued by a copy built from new matter.
On the biological view a digital emulation is not the same organism, so you do not survive.
Psychological continuity is preserved by the teletransporter, though some psychological theorists require the normal cause.
Pushing is generally held to be harder to justify than switching; permitting the push while forbidding the switch reverses this.
Act consequentialism says to push when five lives outweigh one; rule consequentialists can disagree.
Abstract possible worlds are abstract objects, which nominalism denies.
Transcendent universals are abstract objects existing outside space and time.
Structured propositions are usually construed as abstract objects, though some nominalists reconstrue them.
Mereological nihilism denies that statues and lumps exist at all, so it cannot count two of them.
Reliabilism makes justification depend on the external reliability of belief-forming processes; it is the paradigm externalist theory.
Descriptivism about reference ties a name's contribution to associated descriptions, which Millianism rejects.
A hedonist about well-being has prudential reason to enter; refusing can still rest on non-prudential reasons.
If races are unreal, preserving race categories is in tension, though some argue for preserving them for political purposes.
